summary: Presidio EmailRecognizer did not match email addresses with punycode (xn--) domain labels (ETB-06)
details:
`EmailRecognizer` in `presidio-analyzer` matched the domain part of an address with a pattern that allowed a hyphen only when a word character came right after it. A punycode label such as `xn--80ak6aa92e` has two hyphens in a row, so the match failed. An address like `user@xn--80ak6aa92e.com` returned no `EMAIL_ADDRESS` result, while an ordinary ASCII address was detected. This is ETB-06 (missing normalization): an encoded form of an address evaded a detector that compares raw text. The form of the address is chosen by whoever writes the text under analysis. Where the recognizer screens the output of a model or agent, that writer is the system being checked. The etb-scan evidence table lists this pull request under ETB-06.

Fix: pull request #2077 (opened 2026-06-18, merged 2026-06-24, first released in presidio-analyzer 2.2.363 on 2026-06-28) changes the domain pattern to allow hyphen groups inside a label. It adds test cases for punycode addresses and for text that must still not match.

database_specific.note: 'introduced: 0' is a conservative bound. Git tag 2.2.362 does not contain the fix commit and tag 2.2.363 does (GitHub compare, 2026-11-12). PyPI lists 2.2.363, uploaded 2026-06-28.

attack.description: Text contains an email address whose domain is written in punycode. The recognizer returns no result for it, so the address passes through unredacted.
attack.preconditions: The default `EmailRecognizer` pattern. Ordinary ASCII addresses were detected before and after.
attack.poc_pointer: Punycode cases added to presidio-analyzer/tests/test_email_recognizer.py by pull request #2077.

hardening.fix: Allow hyphen groups inside a domain label so punycode labels match, and keep tests for both the new matches and the non-matches.
hardening.pattern: Normalize both trigger strings and model output before matching (taxonomy ETB-06 fix pattern).
hardening.residual_risk: The fix widens the pattern. It does not decode or normalize addresses, so other encoded or obfuscated forms are outside it.

disclosure.tier_reason: Public artifact, no non-public information, impact limited to the detector's result, fix supplied with the report.
disclosure.notes: Reported as pull request #2077 from the AUTHENSOR account, carrying the fix. Approved and merged by a maintainer.
